Question 1
?
Find g′(x) if g(x)=3csc⁡(x)+sin⁡(x).
g′(x)=
−3csc(x)cot(x)+cos(x)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

g′(x)=ddx(3csc⁡(x)+sin⁡(x))=3(−csc⁡(x)cot⁡(x))+cos⁡(x)=−3csc⁡(x)cot⁡(x)+cos⁡(x)

\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5-2\operatorname{csc}⁡x}{{e}^{x}}) \\  & =\frac{(2\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x){e}^{x}-(5-2\operatorname{csc}⁡x){e}^{x}}{({e}^{x})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}(2\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x-5+2\operatorname{csc}⁡x)}{{e}^{2x}} \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x+2\operatorname{csc}⁡x-5}{{e}^{x}}\end{aligned}
$$

q-31288.name: Question 3
q-31288.worked_solution:
First, we just take the constant out of the derivative and use the result for the derivative of $\operatorname{cot}⁡x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-6\operatorname{cot}⁡x) \\  & =-6(-{csc}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =6{csc}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =6{csc}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =6{(2)}^{2} \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(11\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(11\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x+{x}^{-1}) \\  & =11(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =-11\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\sqrt{3}) & =-11\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{sec}⁡(\sqrt{3})\operatorname{tan}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\frac{1}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}} \\  & =-11\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{sec}⁡(\sqrt{3})\operatorname{tan}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the slope of y=f(x) at x=3 if f(x)=11cos⁡x−sec⁡x+1x.

a
11sin⁡(3)−sec⁡(3)tan⁡(3)−13
b
−sin⁡(3)−csc⁡(3)cot⁡(3)−13
c
−11sin⁡(3)+sec⁡(3)tan⁡(3)+13

−11sin⁡(3)−csc⁡(3)cot⁡(3)−1
e
−11sin⁡(3)−sec⁡(3)tan⁡(3)−13

Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we calculate the derivative using the sum rule:

f′(x)=ddx(11cos⁡x−sec⁡x+1x)=ddx(11cos⁡x−sec⁡x+x−1)=11(−sin⁡x)−sec⁡xtan⁡x−1x2=−11sin⁡x−sec⁡xtan⁡x−1x2

Then, we substitute x=3 in the derivative and get f′(3)=−11sin⁡(3)−sec⁡(3)tan⁡(3)−1(3)2=−11sin⁡(3)−sec⁡(3)tan⁡(3)−13.
